transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-05 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Clarke (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood Solutions), Lena Ortiz (Orion Head of Data), Samir Patel (Orion CTO), Jules Rivera (Orion ML Eng), Tom Wu (Orion Security)

Summary:
High-level discovery to decide whether Orion will start with Redwood Hosted for quick pilot vs Dedicated/Private for long-term EU data residency and latency needs. Focus on model choices (open models), context window needs for long manifests, multilingual support, and tool-calling/knowledge retrieval for manifests and routing. Agreed next steps include sending pricing, security pack, and scheduling benchmark.

Topics covered:
- Current infra and constraints (on-prem connectors, EU residency)
- Typical convo/context length (manifest + instructions ~6-12k tokens)
- Model family comparison: Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B/7B-Instruct, Falcon-40B, and larger quantized variants
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs and batching strategies
- Tool calling: retrieval + actions (UPS API, scheduling), function-calling reliability
- Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Security: SOC2/ISO, KMS, SSO, audit logs, data retention

Action items (recap in call):
- Redwood to send pricing and security pack
- Redwood to set up benchmark/run on sample logs
- Orion to prepare sample data and compliance constraints

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Clarke: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um 16:00 UTC, appreciate you carving out time. quick round robin?
[00:06] Lena Ortiz: hey lena here - i'll be the main contact on the data side.
[00:09] Samir Patel: samir, cto. we're evaluating options for our AI assistant across operations.
[00:12] Jules Rivera: jules, ml eng, i'll run the bench stuff.
[00:15] Tom Wu: tom, security - i'll ask the compliance q's.
[00:17] Ethan Clarke: great. priya from infra can you intro real quick?
[00:20] Priya Nair: yeah hi all. i lead infra integrations and latency tuning at redwood. we'll talk models and perf tradeoffs.
[00:25] Marcus Lee: and i'm marcus - solutions, happy to cover pricing outline and dedicated options.
[00:30] Lena Ortiz: quick context: we manage freight manifests and driver instructions, long documents, some multimodal references in future. priority is to automate routing and answer complex queries. data residency EU-first.
[00:42] Ethan Clarke: perfect, thanks. two main axes — speed/time-to-value vs control and residency. for pilot most customers start hosted to iterate, then move to dedicated or private if they need on-prem or VPC control.
[00:55] Samir Patel: our rough target is sub-250ms token latency for short interactions, but for longer reasoning across manifests we care more about throughput and supporting 6k-12k token contexts. is that realistic?
[01:10] Priya Nair: yeah. two parts: if you need 6-12k context, we can either pick models with native window size (eg some variants of falcon/llama w/32k) or use Redwood's prefix/KV cache and chunking. caching helps when users reuse same manifest prefixes.
[01:30] Jules Rivera: question — which open models do you recommend for multilingual (we need EN, ES, PT, and occasional JA) and for tool calling reliability?
[01:40] Priya Nair: short answer: Mistral-7B-instruct or Llama-2-13B for cost-sensitive; Falcon-40B or curated 70B variants for better reasoning at higher cost. multilingual is mixed — some models are stronger in Spanish (mistral family) while others struggle in Japanese. we'd recommend a small eval across your language set. tool-calling works across models with our structured tool schema; reliability depends on prompt design and whether you run in a streaming mode.
[02:08] Jules Rivera: mmm, okay. can you quantify cost delta hosted vs dedicated?
[02:12] Marcus Lee: rough numbers on pricing we'll send, but high-level: hosted is pay-as-you-go, easy but unit $/token is higher vs reserved Dedicated which saves up to 40-60% for sustained throughput. also dedicated gives predictable latency and isolation which helps compliance.
[02:30] Tom Wu: on the security side: we need SOC2 type II, ISO27001, audit logs, and KMS integration — can Redwood do customer-managed keys in Private mode?
[02:42] Priya Nair: yes - Private (VPC/on-prem) supports customer KMS/HSM and we can restrict egress. Dedicated supports customer key options too, but for full air-gapped on-prem you go Private. we'll attach our compliance pack.
[02:58] Samir Patel: about model ops — how do you manage model variants and rollouts? we want canary model swaps and ability to pin versions per-route.
[03:07] Ethan Clarke: redwood has model versioning and rollout policies in the console — canary, A/B, auto-fallback to smaller variants on OOM or latency spikes. console exposes per-route routing policies and token-level cost.
[03:22] Lena Ortiz: we also need strong evals — we will have a 2000-case prompt set to check regressions. do you support regression alerts?
[03:30] Priya Nair: yep, Optimize ties eval sets to monitors and sends regression alerts if metrics drop. we can also run batch evaluations during model upgrades.
[03:38] Jules Rivera: technical nit: our manifests are often 8k tokens after preprocessing. we prefer not to chunk too aggressively because that breaks context. what's the longest native context you support?
[03:48] Priya Nair: native windows depend on model. many open models have 8k or 32k variants; we also support KV cache and prefix caching which lets you keep large static manifests in cache and only stream deltas to model, saving tokens and cost. for 8-12k, either pick a 32k model or use caching with 8k model and tune chunking.
[04:10] Samir Patel: latency with caching — any rough numbers?
[04:12] Priya Nair: it depends on batch sizes. single-request latency w/ a smaller model can be under 200-300ms for short prompts; with large 40B models thats often 500ms-1s. caching reduces token compute but initial cache fill has cost. we'll show benchmarks.
[04:30] Tom Wu: about tool calling — we plan to call an internal routing microservice and a shipment update API. how deterministic is function-calling? we've seen hallucinated function calls elsewhere.
[04:45] Priya Nair: function-calling is more deterministic if you use structured schemas and validation. we recommend a verification step — Redwood can return structured JSON and you run a quick schema validator before executing. we also support chained tool flows in the runtime. occasional hallucination happens with some open models, we'll recommend model+prompt combos that minimize it and fallback checks.
[05:08] Jules Rivera: do you support retrieval-augmented generation? we have an internal vector DB (pinecone-like) and S3 store for docs.
[05:15] Priya Nair: yes - Redwood supports RAG pipelines; we have connectors for common vector DBs and S3. Retriever results can be inserted as tools or memory; you can choose chunking configs.
[05:28] Samir Patel: how about quantization? we want to reduce instance sizes for Dedicated.
[05:32] Priya Nair: we provide quantized model variants and guidance. Dedicated can run int8/int4 quantized kernels which drop memory and cost but may slightly affect quality. Optimize suggests quantization per workload.
[05:45] Lena Ortiz: EU data residency — if we host in EU region but use Redwood Hosted control plane in US, is that an issue for audits?
[05:55] Ethan Clarke: that is a common question. Hosted can keep inference data in EU regions if you pick EU region endpoints; control plane metadata might be in Redwood control plane — for strict audits customers pick Dedicated with EU-only control plane or Private with on-prem. we'll surface exact data flows in the security pack.
[06:12] Tom Wu: we need to see network diagrams and acceptance criteria for encryption in transit and at rest.
[06:18] Ethan Clarke: we'll include diagrams, KMS notes, and our SOC2 reports.
[06:22] [pause / background noise]
[06:30] Marcus Lee: quick on price vs perf — many customers do pilot hosted with Llama-2-13B or Mistral-7B-instruct for routing UX, then run a Dedicated pilot for Falcon-class for heavy reasoning.
[06:45] Jules Rivera: any gotchas with streaming or long outputs for manifests? sometimes streaming breaks structured JSON output.
[06:52] Priya Nair: true — streaming is great for latency but you should only stream when you don't need strict atomic JSON. when you need structured return, use non-streamed function-calling or include end tokens. we also have a strict-output mode that buffers and validates.
[07:10] Samir Patel: let's talk scale — we expect peak 120 qps with bursts to 400 qps during enterprise windows. can Dedicated autoscale?
[07:22] Priya Nair: Dedicated has configurable autoscaling and burst pools; you can reserve baseline capacity and allow short bursts which spin up extra nodes. we also offer SLA-backed throughput tiers for enterprise.
[07:33] Lena Ortiz: what's the SLA for latency and uptime on Dedicated?
[07:36] Marcus Lee: typical Dedicated SLAs are 99.9% uptime with latency targets per model tier. exact numbers depend on committed capacity; we'll share an example SLA in the doc.
[07:46] Tom Wu: okay, about legal/procurement — we need DPA and standard enterprise contract templates to start procurement.
[07:52] Ethan Clarke: we'll share DPA and procurement templates; for Private or Dedicated there are enterprise terms.
[07:58] [09:00-ish small cross talk as someone drops connection briefly]
[08:10] Jules Rivera: technical: for the benchmark run, can you provide a docker image or a reproducible script? we want to measure p99 latencies and token cost.
[08:19] Priya Nair: yes we'll provide benchmark harness (docker+script), and sample model configs. we'll also run a co-located run with you so we can debug.
[08:27] Samir Patel: on multilingual model pick, do you recommend a multi-model strategy per language?
[08:33] Priya Nair: some customers route Spanish to a model stronger in Spanish and English to another model; Redwood supports per-route routing so that's straightforward. routing increases ops complexity but can be automated in the console.
[08:45] Lena Ortiz: what's the expected start timeline? we aim for a pilot in 3 weeks if procurement moves fast.
[08:50] Ethan Clarke: achievable — pilot in 3 weeks on Hosted, or 6-8 weeks for Dedicated setup depending on provisioning. Private/on-prem longer.
[08:58] Tom Wu: any concerns with our current infra — we run GCP in eu-west1, a mix of k8s and some legacy VMs.
[09:06] Priya Nair: sounds fine. for Dedicated we can colocate in eu-west1 or set up VPC peering to avoid egress. for Private we do a dedicated appliance/helm chart for on-prem.
[09:17] Jules Rivera: let's confirm the sample benchmark plan: we want p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost breakdown, and a regression test against our 2k prompts.
[09:25] Priya Nair: yes, we'll include those metrics.
[09:27] Ethan Clarke: ok wrapping up — recap next steps (see action items). schedule bench for week of 3/16. pricing, soc2/docs to you by 3/8-3/9.
[09:38] Samir Patel: great thanks.
[09:40] Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone.
[09:42] Tom Wu: bye.
